subject: ARTE
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: ARTE
courses.title: The Graphic Novel
courses.description: Explores the word-and-image medium of comics as a narrative form. Focuses on the contemporary phenomenon of the so-called graphic novel. What are the preoccupations of today’s graphic novels? How does their storytelling work? Some work in translation is included, but the course largely concentrates on the American tradition, focusing on fiction, memoir, and nonfiction reporting and adaptation. Offers students an opportunity to learn practices of reading—and making—comics. Emphasizes the formal language, or grammar, of comics in order to interpret its narrative procedure and possibilities.

courses.subject: ARTE
courses.title: Art and Design Abroad: Studio
courses.description: Offers an intensive studio course taken abroad and taught by an art and design faculty member. Exposure to regional artists, history, culture, museums, architecture, and physical geography provide focus of study and creative exploration. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: ARTE
courses.title: Art and Design Abroad: History
courses.description: Offers an intensive history course taken abroad and taught by an art history, design, or art faculty member. Exposure to regional and international artists, history, culture, museums, landscape architecture, galleries, material culture, and architecture provide a rich context for studying the history of art and design. Offers students an opportunity to understand narrative and visual components through detailed hands-on workshops and detailed creation of artistic formats, including design, text essays, photographic essays, temporary exhibitions, video art projections, and live performances as artifacts. May be repeated without limit.

courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Offers the candidate, working with a thesis advisor, an opportunity to continue to complete the research project defined and proposed in ARTE 7100. The research is carried out in an independent manner, with periodic presentations to the thesis committee. These presentations define the benchmarks for determination of successful progress in the project. The ultimate result is an exhibition, screening, performance, or other form of public display or presentation, together with a thesis paper or written corollary.
